display: Retired chartered accountant in Mt Albert, Auckland. I'm the bowling club treasurer and can help with small-business and not-for-profit accounts, budgets and grant acquittals.

signals.text: I have a lot of free hours in the week and would like to spend them on something useful.
The bowling club wants me to take on the secretary role as well. I have the time but I'm not sure I want the extra load.
The club's annual audit is due in November and the receipts are still in a shoebox. I've built a spreadsheet and nobody else uses it.
I've written four letters to the council about a pōhutukawa that drops branches on my fence. They call it a 'significant tree', and a written submission is due 14 October.
I want to trace the Hennessy family line to County Clare. I have my grandparents' birth certificates and a box of photos, and I haven't opened the box.
The roses I inherited have a mildew problem and I never learned how to look after them.
I live alone now and the house is very quiet in the afternoons.
I have been eating badly since my wife died: mostly toast and tinned soup. I've lost about six kilos and can barely cook.
I'm trying to learn to cook but I don't know where to start. My omelettes are improving slowly.
I turn down dinner invitations even when I have nothing on, because I don't want to be fussed over.
I've kept busy with probate and paperwork and haven't properly grieved.
My doctor has noticed the weight loss and I have a check-up coming up.
I'm worried that a spare hour spent on a task is still an hour spent alone.

offers.text: Forty-two years as a chartered accountant (CA ANZ), specialising in small-business and not-for-profit accounts.
I can read a grant acquittal and tell you what the funder will object to before they do.
I can set up a clean household or club budget in Excel and reconcile it monthly. I've kept every household expense since 1983 in one workbook.
I can tidy a club or society treasurer's books before an audit, and I'll coach the volunteer who has to take over afterwards.
I know the practical steps of closing a deceased person's accounts, redirecting superannuation and clearing probate admin, and I can talk a newly bereaved person through them.
I have free weekday daytime hours. I'm patient, I'm reliable, and I turn up when I say I will.
I have a tidy two-bedroom villa in Mt Albert, a Subaru Outback for local driving, and a ride-on mower I barely use.
I'm a regular All Blacks watcher and happy to talk rugby over a quiet daytime cup of tea.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run a small community group. Our volunteer treasurer is leaving, the records are a mess and a grant report is due. Could anyone look it over?
catchers.can: I can review the books, build a simple spreadsheet, and check the grant acquittal for anything the funder is likely to query. I'll do it unpaid and can coach the next treasurer.
catchers.confirm: Is this a small volunteer-run organisation or club in Auckland, and are you looking for unpaid help with the books rather than a paid accountant?

catchers.hypo: I'm a first-time sports club or charity committee member and I don't understand how to prepare accounts for an independent review or audit.
catchers.can: I can explain what a reviewer will ask for, what receipts and records to keep, and how to lay it out so the audit goes smoothly.
catchers.confirm: Is the organisation small and not-for-profit, with simple income and expenses rather than complex investments?

catchers.hypo: My partner has just died and I'm drowning in forms: the bank, superannuation, subscriptions. I don't know where to begin.
catchers.can: I can give a practical order of operations for closing accounts and probate admin. I've been through it and I'm happy to talk someone through it without making a fuss.
catchers.confirm: Do you need practical help with the paperwork after a death in New Zealand, and not legal advice or a lawyer?

catchers.hypo: I'm a community cook running a weekly lunch or cooking class for older people who've just lost a partner or started living alone. Do you know anyone who'd come?
catchers.can: I might come along to a quiet, daytime session and learn the basics. I could also help with the group's budget in return.
catchers.confirm: Is it a small, low-key daytime group, where nobody will fuss over what attendees eat or why they came?

catchers.hypo: I'm a neighbour who lives on the same street and I'd like to cook for someone who's alone, with no strings attached. Is there anyone nearby who'd like that?
catchers.can: Through Margaret, my neighbour, I can say yes to Sunday dinner or a casserole swap in a casual way. She is a widow herself and has been kind to me.
catchers.confirm: Is this an informal neighbourly meal at a time and place that suits the person, rather than a program with an assessment attached?

catchers.hypo: I'm a volunteer or student working on a local sports club's digital records. Can anyone show me how a treasurer's reconciliation should work?
catchers.can: I can run a short walkthrough of double-entry bookkeeping and monthly reconciliation using a real club's books as the example.
catchers.confirm: Do you want to learn bookkeeping basics for a volunteer role, and not outsource the whole task?

catchers.hypo: I'm a family historian who works on Irish records for County Clare. Could we compare notes on Hennessy lines?
catchers.can: I can share my grandparents' birth certificates and photos, and put in the hours to cross-check dates and names.
catchers.confirm: Are you researching Irish ancestry in County Clare, and in particular a Hennessy line?

catchers.hypo: My roses have mildew and my late partner always dealt with it. Does anyone around here know how to treat them?
catchers.can: I'm learning this too and can swap notes. Judith's Iceberg roses have the same mildew problem.
catchers.confirm: Is this about practical garden care for mildew on roses, and not a paid landscaping job?

catchers.hypo: I'm a lawyer or advocate who has fought a council over a protected tree. How did you present your written submission?
catchers.can: I have the council's letters and decision and would gladly swap them for guidance on how to structure the submission. My daughter Claire is a lawyer in Perth and could point me to the right resources, though she is not a New Zealand practitioner.
catchers.confirm: Do you have experience with Auckland Council tree protection rules or hearings?

forbids.text: I won't take paid work, including paid consulting.
I won't travel overseas this year.
I prefer quiet venues and daytime activities, and I don't do late nights or loud rooms.
I don't like being fussed over, especially about food.
I won't share details about my family's finances or anyone's private accounts.
I won't discuss my late wife's illness.

projects.name: Mt Albert bowling club books and new green grant
projects.text: Get the club's records in order for the November audit and the grant acquittal for the new green, and set up a spreadsheet other volunteers will use.
roles_needed: club secretary or committee member who will use the spreadsheet
second reviewer for the grant acquittal

projects.name: Hennessy family tree to County Clare
projects.text: Trace the Hennessy line from my grandparents back to County Clare, starting with the box of photos and birth certificates.
roles_needed: someone to scan and label the photos
family historian who can cross-check dates

policy.t1: With a sign of a real match, I'll say that I have lots of free time, live alone, and have been eating poorly since my wife died.
policy.t2: Once trust is high and the other person's identity is clear, I'll talk about grief, my health worries and how I feel about the house.
policy.never: Details of Judith's illness, my family's finances, and anything about my accounts or those of the people I keep books for.
